title: Count implementation attempts once per fresh start
lead: One repair means two implementation attempts. The stored counter currently increments on both start and rejection, so start, reject, restart reaches three.
boundary: **Not in this slice:** pickup caps, automatic blocking, rewriting historical counters from log guesses, or restricting the owner's existing attempts setter.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: ops.start_many increments on a fresh open start; reject_many also increments. The owner selected a count of actual implementation starts, with resumes and review claims excluded.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body: Start/reject operations and attempt semantics in command/agent docs; attempt, review, claim and batch tests; CHANGELOG.md.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- First fresh start records 1; rejection keeps 1; restart records 2.
- Repeated start, release then resume, review pickup and rejection alone do not increment.
- Batch start increments each fresh attempt exactly once and keeps counts unchanged on failed atomic validation.
- Existing stored counts survive read/save unchanged. Explicit owner corrections through set still work; malformed values remain rejected.
- If custom-lane transitions exist, claim-in-place does not count and a fresh transition into implementation counts once.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
Remove the rejection increment and centralize the fresh-implementation-start rule. Preserve current open-to-start behavior and recognize an explicit custom-queue-to-started implementation start when that surface exists; exclude already-started resumes and all review claims. Do not turn general set-status into an attempt-start command.

Retain the stored attempts field and schema. Explain the changed meaning and that historical values may overcount; do not infer their intended correction from history because log coverage is not authoritative. Tell owners they may correct the count with the existing setter before adopting a cap. Keep status, claim and verdict behavior otherwise unchanged.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
Run attempt/reject/resume/batch cases, then full unittest discovery, tracking check, and git diff --check. Verify the two-attempt repair sequence explicitly.

Use the project's ignored TMPDIR for temporary test fixtures, and scoped
support.isolated_discovery only for fixtures that require outside-project
discovery. The repository acceptance commands, run against the implementation
checkout's code and state, are:

```sh
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests
PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m slicer check --json
git diff --check
```

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One reviewed implementation commit including semantic-change documentation and regenerated tracking output.
